transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. _____. What brings you in today?

Hi. Um... well, I guess I'm just having trouble relaxing. It feels like I'm constantly running on a motor lately. 

I finish one thing at school, or at home, and... I just immediately jump right into the next thing. I just can't really seem to shut myself off.
Have you also had times when your mood was unusually high or euphoric?
Um... no. I don't think so. Not really. I wouldn't use that word.
Have you had these trouble-relaxing, always-on-the-go symptoms since childhood?

Yeah, I suppose so. Um... my mother used to joke about it. She'd say that even back in elementary school, I was basically trying to teach the class from my seat. I guess I was always getting out of my chair, talking, or... cutting in before the teacher even finished giving directions. So, yes. It's just who I am. It’s been that way long before adulthood... it's not something that just started with this family change.
Did these symptoms start after the family change or other stressful event?

Well... like I said, I've always been this way. But... I guess this specific level of trouble, where it's this hard to manage... that's been going on for about eight months. Since, um... an older relative moved in with us.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things most days?
No... not really. I mean, just normal things, I suppose. But no, I wouldn't say I worry a lot.
Has this been causing problems in your schoolwork, job, or relationships?

Yeah... I suppose it has. Um... at the school, things haven't been great lately. There were some complaints, and... well, they actually put me on a corrective plan. 

And at home... my spouse says I'm making the new caregiving routines harder. That they basically have to manage my energy on top of taking care of everything else. I'm really just trying to help out, but... I don't know, it feels like I'm damaging trust with my colleagues and my family.
Do you often have trouble focusing on details or staying organized?
No... not really. I mean, I keep things in order well enough. Details aren't really the problem.
Since the family change eight months ago, have you been feeling more tense or on edge most days?
No, I wouldn't say that. I don't really feel tense. Just... normal, I guess.
Do you notice that these symptoms get worse mainly when you're dealing with the family change or caregiving stress?
No... I wouldn't say that. It's not really tied to just that. It's... well, it happens at work too, like I said. It doesn't really seem to matter what I'm doing.
Were you having these kinds of attention or activity problems before age 12?

Yeah, I guess so. My mom used to joke about it. She'd say back in elementary school I was basically teaching the class from my seat. I was... always out of my chair, talking, interrupting the teacher before she was done. It's just... always been how I am. It's not some new thing that started with the family stuff.
Do you often lose track of things you need to do or have trouble finishing tasks because your mind wanders?
No... not really. I don't think my mind wanders much. I usually finish what I need to do.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports a longstanding childhood-onset hyperactive/impulsive presentation with persistent restlessness, excessive talking/interrupting, difficulty relaxing, and impairment in school and home functioning. Symptoms were present before age 12 and continued into adulthood, making ADHD, predominantly hyperactive-impulsive presentation the best fit. Anxiety and mood episodes were denied, and the current worsening appears superimposed on a lifelong pattern rather than explained by a psychosocial stressor alone.
